newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Repsol sale seen guaranteed success.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Repsol sale seen guaranteed success.

text.p: The Spanish Cabinet could give the green light on Friday for the sale next month of the state's remaining 10 percent stake in bluechip energy group Repsol.

If approved as expected, analysts said the oil firm sale should do well following the resounding success in February of the state's disposal of its last 20.9 percent stake in telecommunications company Telefonica.
That bumper offer of at least 171 million shares was nine times oversubscribed by small investors.

Repsol's privatisation history, its widespread perception as a quality company and the fact that fewer shares are on offer than with Telefonica, are seen by analysts as solid reasons for the shares to be snapped up.

"Repsol privatisations have always gone well, and in terms of quality it has a good image with the public. The fact that the (share) offer is many times smaller than for Telefonica also removes uncertainties," said Javier Borrachero, analyst at Central Hispano Bolsa in Madrid.

The state's holding in Repsol, mainly involved in the exploration, production, refining and marketing of crude oil, is around 30 million shares. At Thursday's closing price of 5,740 pesetas, the stake was worth about 172 billion pesetas ($1.2 billion).
Another analyst forecast the stock could subsequently soar to 7,200 pesetas on a 12-month time horizon.
"I'm very keen on Repsol. It's very undervalued compared to its European counterparts and after the adjustment in the price after the placement I see it outperforming," he said.
BCH's Borrachero saw the stock at 6,300 pesetas by year-end.
By 1300 GMT on Friday the shares were trading up 70 pesetas, or 1.39 percent, to 5,810. The Ibex-35 index of leading shares was up 0.2 percent to 5,412.82.
Analysts were predicting that the new shares coming to the market should be sold at a price of around 6,000 pesetas, but one analyst said anything above that price could deter investors.
"Above 6,000 pesetas would scare me a little, as with a large retail tranche the price is very important," he said.
The division of the shares among investors is expected to follow the model set by Telefonica, with a large portion of the offer aimed at small Spanish shareholders.
Sources close to the operation told Reuters that around 15 percent would be allocated to employees of the energy giant.
The remaining 85 percent will likely be equally split betweeen financial institutions --with international and domestic entities getting equal weighting-- and retail investors.
But this set-up would be flexible, with more shares offered to that part of the market where demand was strongest. ($ = 145.0 Spanish Pesetas)
